content.text: All preferred elements are satisfied across §§ 13.1–13.3 and § 24.1. No redline needed.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The licence package meets the preferred position in full. § 13.1 grants access rights to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf", covering both the affiliate and contractor elements without any notice condition. § 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable" fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology (extended to Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables by § 14.3), satisfying the perpetual and irrevocable elements. § 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending any licence except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity, so the subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach, and permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by § 24 — and § 24.1 lets Customer assign without consent to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or asset sale. This sits above the fallback, so no redline is warranted. Noted but not flagged here: § 14.2 gives Customer only a "revocable, non-transferable licence" in Deliverables for the Order Form term, which conflicts with §§ 13.2–13.3; that Deliverable ownership/licence term is addressed under the IP rule rather than double-flagged as a licence-scope deviation.
